items.title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
items.summary: El artículo compartido por Hugging Face analiza el sistema de paralelismo de tuberías necesario para escalar modelos recurrentes en profundidad. En estos modelos, donde se utilizan pilas de bloques compartidos varias veces, se propone una solución a las limitaciones del método tradicional 1F1B en la gestión del flujo de datos cíclico.

snapshot.description: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once. items.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?

snapshot.description: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. items.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?

snapshot.description: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). items.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience

snapshot.description: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Embodied-Harness presenta un marco de agente dual que mejora el proceso de ejecución de tareas de manipulación robótica sin actualizar los parámetros del modelo. Su objetivo es superar las limitaciones de los agentes basados ​​en modelos de lenguaje de visión en la gestión de la memoria y la repetición de experiencias con un mecanismo reflector que analiza la evidencia de ejecución.

snapshot.description: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters.
